design_summary.purpose: Adaptive aero control wrapper that exposes firmware-visible configuration/status access, packages metadata-only model requests, validates streamed model responses, supervises timeout and staleness, and arbitrates a bounded safe actuator command path. The top-level is the synthesizable FPGA entry point and the deterministic control wrapper around an external software/GPU surrogate; it does not implement the surrogate itself.
design_summary.operating_model: The RTL operates as a small-register, narrow-stream control shell for the Physical AI application. Firmware programs the cfg_bus window with enable, mode, sequence, geometry reference, velocity setpoint, clamp limits, timeout thresholds, and fallback position. When enabled and not fault-latched, the request packager emits a bounded 128-bit metadata request with valid/ready semantics. The response monitor accepts 128-bit metadata responses, matches sequence and age, flags stale or timeout conditions, and forwards compact recommendation metadata to the safety guard. The safety guard clamps the final actuator command, selects conservative fallback behavior when required, and holds fallback active until fault acknowledgment after the fault condition clears.

external_interfaces.name: cfg_bus_*
external_interfaces.summary: 64-bit firmware-visible register window for configuration writes, status reads, and fault acknowledgment.

external_interfaces.name: model_req_*
external_interfaces.summary: Valid/ready request transport carrying metadata only; valid and data are emitted by RTL, ready is received by RTL.
external_interfaces.directionality: model_req_valid and model_req_data are outputs; model_req_ready is an input.

external_interfaces.name: model_rsp_*
external_interfaces.summary: Valid/ready response transport carrying metadata only; valid and data are received by RTL, ready is emitted by RTL.
external_interfaces.directionality: model_rsp_valid and model_rsp_data are inputs; model_rsp_ready is an output.

external_interfaces.name: actuator_cmd_*
external_interfaces.summary: Compact scalar or packed-vector command driven only by the safety guard and exposed with a valid indication.

external_interfaces.name: status_*
external_interfaces.summary: Timeout, stale, communication, clamp, fallback, request-inflight, and last-sequence status outputs for firmware and system supervision.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_architecture.role: Top-level FPGA wrapper and integration point for control/status, transport, monitoring, safety arbitration, and final actuator command generation.
responsibilities: Expose the synthesizable top-level entry point and real RTL drivers for cfg_bus, model transport, status bits, and actuator command outputs.
Instantiate and interconnect the configuration window, request packager, response monitor, safety guard, and status aggregator.
Preserve the external transport contract: request valid/data flow from RTL to surrogate, response valid/data flow from surrogate to RTL, with ready driven in the opposite direction.
Ensure bounded datapaths, registered handshakes, and separation of packaging, monitoring, and safety stages for FPGA-friendly timing.
interface_notes: clk and reset_n fan out to all child modules.
cfg_bus signals terminate in the configuration window.
model_req_valid and model_req_data are top-level RTL outputs; model_req_ready is a top-level input from the external surrogate side.
model_rsp_valid and model_rsp_data are top-level inputs; model_rsp_ready is a top-level output to the external surrogate side.
actuator_cmd_valid and actuator_cmd_data are top-level outputs driven through the safety guard.
status pins are driven by the status aggregation path and must not be left undriven.
ownership_notes: Top-level owns no new payload definitions or extra ports beyond the spec.
It is descriptive integration only and does not redefine hierarchy or module names.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_cfg_window
responsibilities: Decode compact memory-mapped reads and writes.

Hold and expose configuration fields for enable, mode select, stream velocity setpoint, actuator min/max clamps, request timeout, stale threshold, sequence ID, geometry reference ID, fault acknowledgment, and fallback actuator position.
Collect sticky status inputs from monitoring and safety stages for firmware visibility.
Provide the control values that seed request generation, timeout supervision, and safety arbitration.
interface_notes: cfg_bus_* is the sole firmware access path.
The module drives the configuration outputs used by the request packager and safety guard.
Sticky status inputs are sampled into the register window for readback and software inspection.
A 64-bit register-space contract is preserved without flattening payload history into registers.
ownership_notes: Owns cfg_enable, cfg_mode_select, cfg_stream_velocity_setpoint, cfg_actuator_min_clamp, cfg_actuator_max_clamp, cfg_request_timeout_cycles, cfg_stale_threshold_cycles, cfg_sequence_id, cfg_geometry_ref_id, cfg_fault_ack, and cfg_fallback_actuator_pos.
Owns cfg_bus_rdata and cfg_bus_ready as the real top-level readback/handshake drivers.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_request_packager
module_architecture.role: Metadata-only request stream formatter and launch controller.
responsibilities: Package request metadata into the 128-bit bounded streaming bus.
Use the configuration enable, mode, velocity setpoint, geometry reference ID, and sequence controls to form request content.
Gate request emission based on configuration enable, in-flight state, and launch eligibility.
Manage valid/ready issuance so that requests are only launched when the external model side can accept them.
interface_notes: request_valid and request_data are generated from the local packaging state.
request_accept and request_ready are input-side handshakes used to determine whether a request launch completed or should be held/retried according to the local control flow.
request_seq_current represents the current sequence context used by downstream monitoring and matching logic.
The request payload remains metadata only and is intentionally narrow for timing closure and portability.
ownership_notes: Consumes cfg_enable, cfg_mode_select, cfg_stream_velocity_setpoint, cfg_geometry_ref_id, and cfg_sequence_id from the configuration window.
Does not implement surrogate math, tensor processing, or geometry storage.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_response_monitor
module_architecture.role: Response validator, timeout supervisor, and stale-data detector.
responsibilities: Accept model response metadata over the bounded 128-bit response stream.
Match response sequence to the current request sequence and reject mismatches.
Track request age in cycles and assert timeout or stale conditions when thresholds are exceeded.
Produce compact recommendation metadata for the safety guard when a valid sample is accepted.
Flag communication and late-response conditions deterministically.
interface_notes: model_rsp_valid/model_rsp_data are sampled inputs from the external surrogate transport path.
model_rsp_ready is driven by the RTL to provide backpressure on the response channel.
request_inflight, request_seq_current, and request_age_cycles provide the live request context.
cfg_request_timeout_cycles and cfg_stale_threshold_cycles define the operating envelope for timeout and stale logic.
response_valid_sample indicates that the response metadata passed sequence and age checks and is suitable for downstream safety arbitration.
ownership_notes: Owns response_recommendation, response_last_sequence, response_timed_out, response_stale_fault, response_comm_fault, and response_valid_sample as its local monitoring outputs.
Translates late, malformed, or mismatched responses into deterministic discard/flag behavior without expanding the payload width.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_safety_guard
module_architecture.role: Final actuator arbitration, clamp enforcement, and fallback control stage.
responsibilities: Select between surrogate-guided recommendation and conservative fallback position depending on fault and acknowledgment state.
Clamp the outgoing actuator command to configured min/max bounds and assert clamp_active when saturation occurs.
Drive the final actuator command only from this stage.
Maintain fallback_active behavior until the fault condition clears and fault acknowledgment is observed.
Provide the last-line safety decision that bounds active aero device commands.
interface_notes: Consumes recommendation metadata from the response monitor and configuration clamps/fallback position from the control window.
status_timeout_fault_in, status_stale_fault_in, and status_comm_fault_in inform fault/fallback arbitration.
cfg_fault_ack gates recovery from fallback after the fault condition clears.
actuator_cmd_valid and actuator_cmd_data are the only top-level actuator command drivers and must originate here.
ownership_notes: Owns the real actuator command output path and clamp/fallback indicators.
Implements conservative default behavior without introducing new control ports or broad datapaths.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_status_aggregator
module_architecture.role: Status fan-in and top-level status pin driver.
responsibilities: Collect monitoring and safety status indicators and drive the exposed top-level status outputs.
Preserve sticky fault and state visibility for firmware and system-level supervision.
Keep last_sequence and request_inflight visible at the top level.
interface_notes: Consumes timeout, stale, comm, clamp, fallback, request_inflight, and last_sequence from the internal control path.
Drives the corresponding top-level status pins directly.
Does not alter control policy; it only presents the aggregated state.
ownership_notes: Provides the descriptive home for the top-level status pin drivers.
Maintains separation between monitoring/safety logic and outward-facing status presentation.

interface_summary.intent: Provide the compact 64-bit register-memory control/status window for firmware configuration, readback, and fault acknowledgment.
Seed request formation with the current control settings and sequence context.
Provide safety bounds, conservative fallback position, and recovery acknowledgment control.
Provide timing thresholds for timeout supervision and stale-data detection.
Emit metadata-only model requests with valid/data driven by RTL and ready received from the external software/GPU surrogate path.
Receive metadata-only model responses with valid/data sourced externally and ready driven by RTL for backpressure and acceptance control.
Pass compact recommendation metadata only after sequence and age validation.
Surface monitoring state for firmware-visible status and safety arbitration.
Generate the bounded actuator command and indicate clamp/fallback conditions from the final safety stage.
Drive the exposed status outputs with the aggregated internal control-state summary.

data_flow_summary.details: Firmware writes and reads the cfg_bus window to set enable, mode select, sequence, geometry reference, velocity setpoint, actuator clamp bounds, timeout thresholds, fallback actuator position, and fault acknowledgment. The register window holds the control state and exposes sticky status for readback.

When enabled and eligible, the request packager forms a narrow metadata request containing request identity, sequence context, geometry source identifier, flow summary/control metadata, and control flags. The package is emitted through a bounded valid/ready request stream with the directionality required by the external model transport contract.

The response monitor accepts metadata-only model responses, verifies sequence correspondence, checks age against the configured thresholds, and deterministically discards late, malformed, or mismatched responses. Matching responses produce a compact recommendation scalar/vector summary for the safety stage.

Cycle counting begins at request launch and continues until a matching response is accepted or a timeout occurs. Responses arriving after the timeout threshold are rejected and flagged. Stale-data logic uses the current sequence and age to assert stale_fault when the age exceeds the configured stale threshold or when a response is late.

The safety guard selects either the validated surrogate recommendation or the conservative fallback actuator position. It clamps the output to the configured min/max bounds and asserts clamp_active on saturation. The final actuator command is generated only at this stage.

Safe fallback remains active whenever fault conditions require it and persists until fault_ack is observed after the fault condition clears. Sticky status bits preserve visibility of timeout_fault, stale_fault, comm_fault, clamp_active, fallback_active, request_inflight, and last_sequence.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: Single-clock synchronous operation on clk with registered handshakes and narrow datapaths to keep timing closure friendly for modest FPGA targets.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: reset_n is active-low and is distributed to all child modules. On reset, the control, request, response, safety, and status paths return to a known safe state with inactive request/response handshakes, cleared or safe-latched status, and conservative actuator behavior.

integration_notes: The top-level must remain the sole synthesizable entry point named adaptive_aero_control_top.
No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from the spec; this document only describes the existing contract.
The model transport is metadata-only and bounded to 128 bits; no tensor math, ML layers, or large geometry arrays are implied.

Bulk payload/history/FIFO storage, if required by implementation policy, must be described through a technology-neutral memory wrapper that can map to FPGA block RAM rather than being flattened into registers.
Top-level outputs must have real RTL drivers; required outputs are not to be tied only to child inputs.
Late or malformed responses are handled deterministically by discard/reject logic, with stale and timeout status reporting preserved for firmware.
The architecture explicitly supports the architecture-definition mode and cpu_reference deployment path with the surrogate executed in software/GPU outside the RTL wrapper.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
